gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: one calibration per method first, then the NIR and MIR blocks joined with block scaling or autoscaling so that neither block dominates the model. Both probes must look at the same small area of the product and the data must be aligned to a common time step. Each instrument keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the joined model must beat the best single method on independent runs or batches, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
Performance figures for this application: the supplied material gives no accuracy, detection limit or response time for fat or protein in a dairy process stream.
The usable length of a mid-infrared fiber link for an in-line installation is not stated in the supplied material.

items.finding: The source says temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For in-line product temperature at the measurement point, this suggests monitoring or controlling temperature to limit OH-band effects; test whether temperature variation changes NIR/MIR spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement about aqueous solutions and tempered sample holders, not a dairy process stream or an in-line temperature sensor; transfer to opaque concentrated milk needs testing.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source says block scaling is often recommended for data fusion but can sometimes have a worse effect on results than other pre-processing methods.
items.how_it_applies: When joining NIR and MIR blocks, test block scaling or autoscaling against alternatives rather than assuming it improves the joined model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a dairy data-fusion review, not a trial on opaque concentrated milk; the result may depend on the specific blocks and preprocessing.

citation.quote: While block scaling is often recommended for data fusion, sometimes it can have a worse effect on results than other pre-processing methods (17).
citation.label: E03 ¶16

items.finding: The source says SO-PLS is not affected by scaling of each block because it is independent of scaling, so it is not affected by variance differences between data blocks.
items.how_it_applies: Consider SO-PLS as a fusion approach that may avoid scaling sensitivity when combining NIR and MIR blocks; compare it with the best single method on independent runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a method statement from a dairy data-fusion review, not a validation on this product or process; transfer to in-line concentrated milk needs testing.

citation.quote: SO-PLS is not affected by scaling of each block as it is independent of the scaling, therefore is not affected by variance differences between data blocks (22).
